rules.source: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) — https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/privacy-topics/privacy-laws-in-canada/the-personal-information-protection-and-electronic-documents-act-pipeda/
rules.retrieved_snippet: PIPEDA is the federal privacy law for private-sector organizations, setting ground rules for how businesses must handle personal information in commercial activity. In force since April 2000.

rules.source: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada — Privacy and Kids — https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/privacy-topics/information-and-advice-for-individuals/privacy-and-kids/
rules.retrieved_snippet: The OPC considers children under 13 unable to meaningfully consent to data collection. Canada has no dedicated children's privacy statute yet — a Children's Privacy Code was under active public consultation as of this research, existing protection is via PIPEDA's general consent framework plus OPC guidance.

rules.source: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada — Consultation on the Development of a Children's Privacy Code — https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/about-the-opc/what-we-do/consultations/completed-consultations/consultation-children-code/
rules.retrieved_snippet: OPC ran a formal consultation (37 stakeholder submissions) on developing a dedicated children's privacy code; no such code is finalized law yet as of this research — flag as an evolving area, not settled statute.

The Competition Act's purposes include providing consumers with competitive prices and product choices; the Competition Bureau enforces it, and it incorporates the Consumer Packaging and Labelling Act and Textile Labelling Act.

rules.source: No enacted comprehensive federal AI statute as of September 2026 — the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA, part of Bill C-27) died on the Order Paper when Parliament was prorogued 6 January 2025 and has not been reintroduced. The current federal Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation has stated a future framework would be introduced separately, not as AIDA revived. What actually applies today: PIPEDA (general privacy law, already covered above), Quebec's provincial Law 25, and sector-specific guidance (e.g. OSFI E-23 for federally regulated financial institutions) — https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovation-better-canada/en/artificial-intelligence-and-data-act-aida-companion-document
rules.retrieved_snippet: AIDA never became law; Bill C-27 died on the Order Paper 6 January 2025. Canada has no comprehensive AI-specific law in force as of 2026.

rules.source: Accessible Canada Act (ACA), S.C. 2019, c. 10 — Royal Assent 21 June 2019, in force 11 July 2019 — https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/A-0.6/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Applies to the federal public sector and federally regulated organizations (banking, telecommunications, transportation, broadcasting) — not a general private-sector requirement. Covered organizations must publish accessibility plans; as of 31 May 2024, federal entities must comply with EN 301 549, which incorporates WCAG 2.1 Level AA plus provisions for non-web software and mobile apps.
